note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), read offline from the bundled owb-am text, per the founder decision of 2026-11-18 that every Amharic work quotes OWB. Every quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim, replacing the 1962 UBS wording and the OT renderings made in its register: the text and its repetitions, Spurgeon's chains of gospel invitations, and the verses he recites inside his own sentences without quotation marks (Isaiah 38:1, Amos 4:12, Genesis 19:17, Isaiah 55:11, the 'highways and hedges' of the text).

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse or range, the shortest span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'. Where OWB is quoted inside someone's speech, the inner marks are ‹ ›. `self_rendered` rows (each with a `why`) are allusions, the author's own paraphrases, and his own summary sentences that the English sets in quotation marks.

Judgement calls. The text, Luke 14:23 'Compel them to come in', is OWB «ሰዎች እንዲገቡ አጥብቀህ ለምናቸው» ('press them to come in'), quoted that way wherever Spurgeon quotes or recites it (decision compel). Because the whole sermon argues from 'compel' (ግድ ማለት), the first prose quotation of the text (block 2) carries a one-time gloss naming the older rendering ግድ በላቸው and calling the pleading strong enough to compel; Spurgeon's own 'I compel you' prose keeps ግድ. The sermon's title keeps its established wording ይገቡ ዘንድ ግድ በላቸው (a title, not a quotation in the body) — raised for the founder. 1 Timothy 1:15 'chief of sinners' is OWB «ከእነርሱም ሁሉ የከፋው» ('the worst of them'); the objector's later 'I am the chief of sinners' (block 27) stays the translator's because Spurgeon argues from 'chief' there. Acts 13:26 'Unto you is the word of salvation sent' is OWB «ይህ የመዳን ቃል ወደ እኛ ተልኳል» ('to us'). 'As I live … no pleasure in the death of him that dieth' is quoted from Ezekiel 33:11, the verse carrying 'As I live'. Genesis 19:17 is plural in OWB, so the surrounding exhortation in block 22 follows it into the plural. Hebrews 10:28-29, Proverbs 1:24-26 and Matthew 25:41 are joined from exact OWB pieces as Spurgeon abridges them; Matthew 25:41 drops his added 'in hell'.
